$comment: Single source of truth for what Smarvii can analyse. Edit this file only, then run `node registry/sync.mjs` to copy it into the worker and web app. Bump registry_version on every change. Each analysis run records the version it was produced with; past reports are never reinterpreted under a newer version.

status_definitions.validated: Measured against a held-out evaluation set and met the acceptance thresholds written down before the run.
status_definitions.experimental: Available in the product, clearly labelled, every result needs human review. Not yet validated.
status_definitions.proposed: Researched and specified, not built. Manual review only for now.
status_definitions.unavailable: Cannot be produced from phone or glasses video with the current pipeline. Never shown as a number.
status_definitions.manual: No automated analysis. People add events and notes by hand.

metric_kinds.observable_event: Something that happened at a time you can point to in the video (a rep, a swing, a punch).
metric_kinds.qualitative_observation: A visible coaching note tied to a timestamp. Words, not numbers.
metric_kinds.measurement: A number with a unit derived from the video. Needs a validated method; language-model estimates never count.
metric_kinds.contextual_outcome: The result of an event that depends on context outside the athlete (contact, target hit). Always human-confirmed.

activities.label: Strength and gym reps
activities.training_question: How many reps did I do of each movement, and where in the video is each one?

events.definition: One full cycle of the named movement, from start position back to start position.

metrics.label: Rep count
metrics.definition: Number of completed rep events after review.

metrics.label: Rep start and end times
metrics.definition: Video timestamps bounding each rep; a reviewer can adjust them.

metrics.label: Movement name
metrics.definition: The movement seen (for example hinge, lunge, squat). The reviewer corrects it.

metrics.label: Technique note
metrics.definition: A visible cue tied to a timestamp, for example hips travel back before the knees bend.

not_available.reason: Needs calibrated capture or a sensor; frame sampling cannot measure it.
2D pose agreement with marker-based capture depends on viewing angle and joint, and is weak for small motions.

not_available.metric: Load, range of motion in cm, power
not_available.reason: Not observable from video without calibration or equipment data.

capture.view: Side-on for hinges and squats, the whole body in frame, camera steady.
capture.glasses: Good when the wearer films someone else; poor for the wearer's own reps.

failure_cases: Camera motion or turning away mid-set
Equipment or other people blocking the athlete
Movement description missing or not matching the video
review_controls: Add, delete, split or move any rep
Confirm who the recording shows before publishing

evaluation.dataset: fixtures/gym (2 real clips; labels kept in fixture files only)

activities.label: Any described movement
activities.training_question: How many times did I do the movement I described?

events.definition: One repetition as the user defines it in the movement description.

metrics.label: Rep count
metrics.definition: Number of completed reps of the described movement after review.

not_available.metric: Any speed, distance, angle or force

capture.view: Whole body in frame, camera steady, one person moving.

failure_cases: Vague or missing movement description (the analysis abstains)
Movements where what counts as one rep is ambiguous
review_controls: Add, delete, split or move any rep
Confirm who the recording shows before publishing

activities.label: Softball hitting
activities.training_question: How many swings did I take, and which made contact?

events.definition: A full swing attempt. Bunts and checked swings are excluded.

metrics.label: Swings
metrics.definition: Number of swing events after review.

metrics.label: Contact result
metrics.definition: Fair contact, foul, swing and miss, or unclear. Shown as counts out of swings, never as a batting average.

not_available.metric: Bat speed, swing time, exit velocity, launch angle
not_available.reason: Published swing kinematics used 300 Hz cameras with calibration; 30 fps phone or glasses video cannot resolve a ~0.2 s swing.

capture.view: Side-on from the first-base side for right-handed hitters, third-base side for left-handed.
capture.glasses: Usable from the coach's position; the ball is often lost.

review_controls: Confirm who the recording shows before publishing

activities.label: Underhand softball pitching
activities.training_question: How many pitches did I throw, and how many hit the target?

events.definition: One delivery from the start of the windmill to release.

metrics.label: Pitches
metrics.definition: Number of pitch events after review.

metrics.label: Target result
metrics.definition: Target hit, missed or unclear, against the target the coach described. Shown as counts out of pitches.

not_available.metric: Pitch speed, spin rate, release angle
not_available.reason: Needs radar or high-speed calibrated capture.

capture.view: Behind or beside the catcher with the target in frame.
capture.glasses: Usable when the target stays in view.

review_controls: Confirm who the recording shows before publishing

activities.label: Tennis strokes
activities.training_question: How many strokes did I hit in this drill, and of which kind?

events.definition: One racket swing at the ball, from backswing to follow-through.

metrics.label: Strokes
metrics.definition: Number of stroke events after review.

metrics.label: Stroke group
metrics.definition: Forehand, backhand or serve only. Finer classes (slice, volley, smash) are not offered: published RGB models confuse them without the ball.

metrics.label: Serve technique note
metrics.definition: Visible cues such as knee bend before the drive or trunk rotation, worded as observations for the coach to confirm.

not_available.metric: Ball speed, spin, racket speed, in or out calls
not_available.reason: Needs radar, high-speed or multi-camera tracking.
2D angles need the camera perpendicular to the plane of motion, and agreement varies by view and joint.

capture.view: Behind the baseline or side-on, the whole player in frame.
capture.glasses: Poor for the wearer's own strokes; usable when a coach films.

failure_cases: Serve and smash look alike without the ball

evaluation.dataset: needs consented tennis clips; THETIS is an indoor, ball-less research set

activities.label: Boxing pad, bag and shadow work
activities.training_question: How many punches did I throw in this round, and of which kind?

events.definition: One punch from guard to full extension and back.

metrics.label: Punches
metrics.definition: Number of punch events after review.

metrics.label: Punch type
metrics.definition: Jab, cross, hook or uppercut, lead or rear, for a coach to confirm. No published baseline accuracy exists yet for this labelling.

not_available.reason: Validated values come from glove sensors at 1000 Hz checked against a force plate, not from video.
Needs two-person tracking and contact judgement; multi-athlete tracking is experimental and identity is never inferred from appearance.

capture.view: Fixed camera, front-oblique, one boxer in frame.
capture.glasses: Unsuitable for the wearer's own punches; usable for a coach holding pads only if the boxer stays in view.

failure_cases: Arms hidden by the bag or a partner

evaluation.dataset: needs consented clips; BoxingVI lists public videos and labels

activities.label: Anything else (manual review)
activities.training_question: Keep the video with timestamped notes and a coach's or your own review.
review_controls: Add events and notes by hand

sources.citation: Dwibedi, Aytar, Tompson, Sermanet, Zisserman. Counting Out Time: Class Agnostic Video Repetition Counting in the Wild. CVPR 2020.
sources.finding: On the Countix test set (YouTube clips), mean relative count error 0.364 and about 30% of clips off by more than one rep. Counts can halve when two body parts repeat at different rates.

sources.citation: Menychtas et al. Gait analysis comparison between manual marking, 2D pose estimation algorithms, and 3D marker-based system. Frontiers in Rehabilitation Sciences 4:1238134, 2023.
sources.finding: 2D pose tracks large joint motion comparably to marker capture but struggles with small motions such as the ankle.

sources.citation: Baldinger, Reimer, Senner. Influence of the Camera Viewing Angle on OpenPose Validity in Motion Analysis. Sensors 25(3):799, 2025.
sources.finding: Joint angles differ significantly by camera viewing angle; shoulder agreement was poor.

sources.citation: Vinyes Mora, Knottenbelt. Deep Learning for Domain-Specific Action Recognition in Tennis. CVPR Workshops (CVSports) 2017.
sources.finding: On THETIS RGB video, 47% accuracy for 12 stroke classes, 77% for 4 stroke groups, 88% for 3 strokes; serve and smash confused without the ball.

sources.citation: Cai, Tang. RGB Video Based Tennis Action Recognition Using a Deep Weighted Long Short-Term Memory. arXiv:1808.00845, 2018.
sources.finding: 74% on THETIS 12 classes under a different (5-fold) protocol; authors call for tests on real match video.

sources.citation: Elliott. Biomechanical Analysis of Stroke Production. ITF Coaching & Sport Science Review 50:7-9, 2010. CC BY 4.0.
sources.finding: Observe hip-shoulder rotation, racket path, knee flexion before the serve drive; 2D angle measurement needs the camera perpendicular to the motion.

sources.citation: Kumar et al. BoxingVI: A Multi-Modal Benchmark for Boxing Action Recognition and Localization. arXiv:2511.16524, 2025.
sources.finding: 6,915 punch clips in 6 classes from fixed monocular video with 2D pose for one boxer; dataset only, no baseline accuracy.

sources.citation: Menzel, Potthast. Validation of a Unique Boxing Monitoring System. Sensors 21(21):6947, 2021.
sources.finding: Glove force sensors at 1000 Hz agreed with a force plate (R = 0.995, RMSE 59.8 N) for two boxers; force and speed came from sensors, not video.

sources.citation: Reilly-Boccia, Ficklin, Lund. Swing Kinematics Described in Division I Female Softball Players. The Sport Journal, 2015.
sources.finding: Bat velocity (28.8 m/s) and swing time (0.21 s) were measured with 300 Hz cameras and a calibration distance; no validity statistics reported.

sources.citation: Lincoln, Ill, Ibrahim. Progressive Strategies for Teaching Fundamental Resistance Training Movement Patterns. NSCA Personal Training Quarterly 10.2, 2023.
sources.finding: Hinge cues (push hips back), one or two cues at a time, model from front and side, video as augmented feedback.
